newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice market steady, export business light.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice market steady, export business light.

text.p: Vietnam's rice export prices have held steady over the past week, but with buyers looking to Pakistan and Thailand rice, business was very light, traders said on Thursday.

They said five percent broken grade was currently trading at around $280-$285 a tonne FOB Saigon Port, unchanged from levels a week ago. Ten percent broken rice was trading slightly lower at $270-$275 a tonne.
"There's really been very little activity out of Saigon Port, maybe a little offtake to Africa," said one trader. "Really, prices are better elsewhere."
Traders said there were still signs that paddy from the main producing area, the flood-stricken Mekong Delta, was in thin supply possibly because of lingering transport problems.
They added that some farmers had harvested early ahead of the flood season, leaving a long delay before the next crop.
This year's flooding was reported to be the worst in more than two decades, and traders say the next harvest in southern Vietnam was likely to be delayed until March.
Current interest in Vietnamese rice was reported to be coming from African nations, with Sri Lanka remaining a significant buyer of 25-percent broken grade.
